title: Cap. IV Arg. 2: Heb. 11:6 — without that by which one cannot please God, none can be elected
pass_a_gloss: Argument 2. Second they argue from the words of the Apostle, Heb. 11:6. Without faith it is impossible to please God. Whence they construct such an argument; Without that without which it is impossible to please God, without it it is impossible that anyone be elected by God to salvation: Without faith it is impossible to please God: Therefore. They pronounce the Major certain, inasmuch as to elect to salvation is the highest love which God can show to a man, or his greatest love in a man.
pass_b_english: Arg. 2. Second they argue from Heb. 11:6 — Without faith it is impossible to please God — and build this: Without that without which one cannot please God, no one can be elected by God to salvation; without faith one cannot please God; therefore. They call the Major certain, since electing to salvation is the highest love God can show a man — his greatest love toward a man.
source_text: Arg. 2. Secundo argumentantur ex verbis Apostoli, Hebr. xi. 6. Sine fide impossibile est placere Deo. Unde tale argumentum exstruunt; Sine quo impossibile est placere Deo, sine eo impossibile est a Deo quenquam eligi ad salutem: Sine fide impossibile est placere Deo: Ergo. Majorem certam esse pronunciant, quandoquidem eligere ad salutem, summa est dilectio quam homini Deus praestare potest, sive maxima ipsius in homine dilectio.
